key_insight: A speech-based multimodal LLM framework that combines audio and transcripts can improve generalizable cognitive impairment detection.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support scalable, non-invasive screening for cognitive impairment while reducing reliance on sensitive raw patient data.
method: Extract acoustic embeddings directly from speech audio.
Generate textual embeddings from automatic speech transcripts.
Concatenate modality-specific features and classify cognitive impairment with open-source LLM-based models.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on ADReSS20 and ADReSSo21 and reported 92.4% CI classification accuracy, outperforming single-modality baselines and improving cross-dataset generalization.
watch_item: Performance may depend on transcript quality and dataset characteristics, so real-world deployment should verify robustness across accents, devices, and clinical settings.
paper_title: Toward Generalizable Cognitive Impairment Detection with Speech-Based Multimodal Large Language Models
